title: Athena End To End Ai Agent
shortDescription: Production-Ready TTS Microservice (Supertonic ONNX) Architecture • Folder Structure • Deployment • Scaling • APIs • Best Practices Fully tuned for AI agent usage. What This Serv...
description: **Athena** is a desktop‑bound, autonomous 3D AI companion that combines a **React/Vite** UI, a custom **Three.js** rendering pipeline for VRM/FBX avatars, and a local AI microservice stack orchestrated by **LangGraph**. The system bridges the Electron main process with background services via IPC, enabling zero‑latency speech‑to‑text (**Whisper‑fast**) and text‑to‑speech (**SuperTonic**, OpenAI, Azure, ElevenLabs) adapters. It leverages **MediaPipe** for face tracking, **Langchain** for tool routing, and supports multiple LLM back‑ends such as **Google Gemini**, **Ollama**, and custom agents via `CustomAgentAdapter`.
longDescription:
**Core Architecture**
Athena runs as an Electron application where the renderer process hosts a Vite‑powered React UI. The UI renders a 3D avatar using a bespoke Three.js engine that manages VRM models, FBX animations, and real‑time lip‑sync via FFT audio analysis. *MediaPipe* provides webcam‑based face tracking to drive eye contact and blinking.

**Data Flow & Microservices**
User speech is captured by the browser Web Speech API or selected STT provider (e.g., `DeepgramSTTAdapter`, `GroqWhisperSTTAdapter`). Audio is streamed to the local **Whisper‑fast** FastAPI service (`POST /stt`) which returns transcriptions. The transcribed text is fed to a **LangGraph** agent (Node.js) that routes requests to LLM providers (Gemini, Ollama, custom) and executes tools such as web search or RAG. Responses are sent to a TTS provider (`POST /tts` on the SuperTonic service) or external services (OpenAI `tts-1`, Azure) and played back, triggering lip‑sync updates.

**Security & Guardrails**
All inter‑process communication is mediated by Electron's `contextBridge` with strict channel whitelisting. Microservices expose minimal HTTP endpoints (`/health`, `/status`) and run on dynamically assigned ports to avoid collisions. API keys for external providers are entered via the settings modal and never persisted to disk.

**Build & Deployment**
The monorepo uses npm workspaces. Frontend assets are bundled with Vite, while backend services are containerized via Docker for reproducible local development. The `npm start` script launches Electron, the React renderer, and the Python/Node microservices concurrently.
myContributions: Architected a modular microservice application using Electron IPC to bridge a Vite React frontend with local Python and Node services.
Developed a custom Three.js rendering pipeline for VRM and FBX models, achieving stable 60 FPS performance.
Implemented deep GPU memory management via `deepDispose` and enforced high‑performance WebGL contexts.
Integrated LangGraph for dynamic tool orchestration, enabling web search, weather, timer, and RAG capabilities.
Built a zero‑latency local voice stack combining Whisper‑fast (STT) and SuperTonic (TTS) with real‑time audio streaming.
Added MediaPipe‑based face and eye tracking to maintain avatar eye contact and natural blinking.
Created FFT‑driven lip‑sync mapping audio frequencies to blendshape weights, reducing CPU overhead.
Designed fallback adapters (`WebSpeechTTSAdapter`, `WebSpeechSTTAdapter`) for browser‑only environments.
Implemented robust event system in `AthenaEngine` for status changes, speech lifecycle, and error handling.
Established a unified `CustomAgentAdapter` allowing plug‑in of arbitrary LLM endpoints with custom request/response transforms.
Designed and implemented a modular microservice architecture using Electron IPC to bridge a Vite React frontend with Python and Node.js background services.
Developed a high‑performance Three.js rendering pipeline for VRM and FBX models, achieving stable 60 FPS.
Created custom memory management (`deepDispose`) for GPU resources and animation data.
Integrated LangGraph to orchestrate tool execution, enabling web search, weather API, timer, and RAG capabilities.
Implemented zero‑latency local speech stack combining Whisper‑fast (Python) for STT and SuperTonic (Node) for TTS.
Added MediaPipe‑based face and head tracking for realistic eye contact and blinking.
Engineered CPU throttling and lip‑sync math mapping audio frequencies to blendshapes to reduce overhead.
Built a flexible adapter system for multiple TTS providers (`OpenAITTSAdapter`, `AzureTTSAdapter`, `WebSpeechTTSAdapter`).
Implemented secure Electron contextBridge with whitelisted IPC channels and dynamic port allocation.
Authored comprehensive SDK documentation covering adapters, React component props, and engine methods.

features: Real‑time 3D avatar rendering with VRM and FBX support.
High‑fidelity text‑to‑speech using SuperTonic with optional cloud providers (OpenAI, Azure, ElevenLabs).
Dynamic tool execution through LangGraph agents (search, weather, timer, RAG).
MediaPipe face tracking for eye contact and blink animation.
FFT‑based lip‑sync that maps audio to facial blendshapes.
Electron IPC bridge that isolates UI from backend services.
Theme support (`dark`, `light`) and customizable avatar model URL.
Graceful fallback to browser Web Speech API when no API keys are provided.
Real‑time 3D avatar rendering with VRM/FBX support.
High‑fidelity text‑to‑speech via multiple adapters (OpenAI, Azure, ElevenLabs, SuperTonic).
LangGraph‑driven tool routing and autonomous decision making.
Dynamic theming and positioning of the Athena widget.
Secure Electron IPC bridge with context isolation.
Configurable API key management for external providers.
challenges: Balancing GPU resource usage while maintaining 60 FPS on varied hardware.
Ensuring low latency between STT, LLM processing, and TTS without blocking the UI thread.
Managing cross‑language communication between Python (Whisper) and Node.js services.
Handling dynamic port allocation to avoid collisions in concurrent development environments.
Providing a seamless fallback to browser‑based Web Speech APIs when external services are unavailable.
learnings: Electron IPC can serve as a performant, secure bridge when combined with strict preload validation.
Local Whisper models deliver acceptable accuracy for desktop use while keeping user data private.
Modular adapter patterns simplify swapping between cloud and on‑device AI services.
FFT‑based lip‑sync offers a good trade‑off between realism and computational cost.
Dynamic service discovery (port negotiation) is essential for developer ergonomics in multi‑service desktop apps.
Modular microservice design simplifies swapping AI providers and scaling components independently.
Deep disposal of Three.js resources is critical for long‑running desktop applications.
Electron's contextBridge can enforce strong security boundaries while still enabling rich IPC.
FFT‑based lip‑sync offers a lightweight alternative to phoneme‑based approaches.
Dynamic port management reduces developer friction when running multiple local services.

remotionVideoScript.voiceoverScript: Welcome to the technical breakdown of athena-end-to-end-ai-agent, a production-grade application engineered with TypeScript, JavaScript, Python. System Architecture & Topology: The application uses a decoupled multi-tier architecture powered by WebSockets, Express, FastAPI on the backend and React, TailwindCSS on the client. Network Routes: The API exposes 4 primary routes including GET /health and POST /tts and GET /status, managing request routing and data serialization. AI Capabilities: Powered by ONNX Runtime, delivering real-time inference and intelligent processing. Performance & Quality: Automated quality checks and clean component patterns ensure high reliability. Explore the full open-source codebase on GitHub at Sameer-Bagul slash athena-end-to-end-ai-agent.
